title: Reflection of polynomials is multiplicative
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T$ an indeterminate. For an integer $N\geq0$ and $Q\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $\deg Q\leq N$, write $[T^k]Q$ for its coefficients [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient] and put

$$
\mathrm{rev}_N(Q)(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{N}[T^k]Q\;T^{N-k}\in R[T].
$$

Then for $Q_1,Q_2\in R[T]$ with $\deg Q_1\leq N_1$ and $\deg Q_2\leq N_2$ one has $\deg(Q_1Q_2)\leq N_1+N_2$ and

$$
\mathrm{rev}_{N_1+N_2}(Q_1Q_2)=\mathrm{rev}_{N_1}(Q_1)\,\mathrm{rev}_{N_2}(Q_2).
$$

Consequently, for $Q_1,\dots,Q_n$ with $\deg Q_j\leq N_j$, $\mathrm{rev}_{N_1+\dots+N_n}(Q_1\cdots Q_n)=\prod_j\mathrm{rev}_{N_j}(Q_j)$ (induction on $n$, with $\mathrm{rev}_0(1)=1$).

source.place: hidden in the identification of the reciprocal roots with multiplicity (no proof given); standard: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV (not in literature/, wanted)
